title: Everyone Skips Chengdu for 'Old China' — It's 2,300 Years Old | China Travel Expert
description:
When travellers want "ancient China," they book Beijing or Xi'an — and quietly skip Chengdu. That's a mistake.

Chengdu is one of the very few major cities on earth to have kept the same name and the same site for over 2,300 years. The kings of the ancient Shu state established their capital here around 311 BC, and the city has sat on this spot ever since — through every dynasty, the Republic, and today.

And it's not a museum piece: teahouses you can sit in all afternoon, some of the fieriest hotpot in the country, and the giant pandas just outside town. One of China's oldest cities is also one of its most relaxed.

So is Chengdu the most underrated old city in China? Tell me where I'm wrong.

★ Expert Tip: build in a slow afternoon at a classic teahouse like He Ming in People's Park — ear-cleaning, tea refills and card games are the whole point of Chengdu.

成都是世界上少数几座两千三百多年名字和城址都没变的大城市之一：古蜀国约公元前 311 年在此建都，至今未迁。茶馆、火锅、城郊的大熊猫——最被低估的中国古城？
